title: Shin Splints
claims: AAOS defines shin splints as medial tibial stress syndrome, an inflammation of muscles, tendons and bone tissue around the tibia, with pain along the inner border of the tibia.
AAOS lists sudden changes in frequency, duration or intensity, flat feet or rigid arches, and worn-out footwear as contributing factors.
AAOS notes stress fracture, tendinitis and chronic exertional compartment syndrome can also cause shin pain and may need to be ruled out.
AAOS advises returning to exercise only after being pain-free for at least 2 weeks, at lower frequency, duration and intensity.
AAOS describes the wet test: a flat foot leaves an impression of the whole foot, while a high arch shows only the ball and heel.
AAOS states there is no clear evidence that barefoot running reduces injury risk.
